evidence_span.text: After successful knockdown of all transcripts (Fig. 5D), cholesterol levels were significantly decreased compared with the control (Fig. 5E).

reviews.rationale: siRNA knockdown of Msmo1(SC4MOL), Nsdhl, and Erg28 causally reduces total cellular cholesterol in human Huh7 liver cells, supporting their C4-demethylation biosynthesis role; Hsd17b7 is gene-specifically profiled but its catalytic contribution appears only as background. Human/hamster cell lines make the mouse-hepatocyte context indirect, so the declared partial is overclaimed.

evidence_span.text: the high intracellular expression ratio of SREBP cleavage-activating protein (Scap) to insulin-induced gene (Insig) disrupted the SREBP2-mediated feedback regulation of cholesterol homeostasis in these cells

reviews.rationale: The abstract links the Scap:Insig expression ratio to disrupted SREBP2 cholesterol feedback, supporting a narrower dysregulated form of the regulator relationship but in hepatic stellate cells, not hepatocytes, and without any supplied program gene. The cell-type mismatch makes the declared direct context an overclaim.

evidence_span.text: Farnesyl diphosphate synthase (FDPs), an integral enzyme in the mevalonate pathway involved in cholesterol biosynthesis, has emerged as a crucial regulator of metabolic homeostasis in cancer

reviews.rationale: Fdps is gene-specifically investigated, but the functional experiments address HCC proliferation via an FDPS-G6PD interaction; its mevalonate/cholesterol-biosynthesis role is asserted only as introductory background, so function is not supported. Human HCC cell lines make the mouse-hepatocyte context indirect.

evidence_span.text: SCAP-deficient mice showed an 80% reduction in basal rates of cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis in liver, owing to decreases in mRNAs encoding multiple biosynthetic enzymes.

reviews.rationale: In vivo conditional SCAP knockout in mouse liver causally reduces cholesterol synthesis and biosynthetic-enzyme mRNAs, directly supporting mechanism 2's claim of SCAP as master regulator of the hepatic program; Scap is a regulator, so no supplied genes are credited. Mouse liver hepatocyte context matches the target for this general mechanism, so direct is accurate.
